examples.title: List open workspaces
examples.purpose: Discover the workspaces that are already available before opening another solution.
examples.expectedOutcome: A bounded inventory of open workspaces, or an empty inventory when none are open.

examples.title: Open a solution
examples.purpose: Load a trusted solution once and assign an alias that later calls can use.
examples.expectedOutcome: The workspace opens and subsequent calls can select it by the sample alias.

examples.workflowTitle: Find and inspect a symbol safely
examples.title: Search a selected workspace with a limit
examples.purpose: Find matching symbols without returning an unbounded result set.
examples.expectedOutcome: At most 25 symbols are returned and hasMore indicates whether the query found additional matches.

examples.workflowTitle: Find and inspect a symbol safely
examples.title: Find references using a stable symbol selector
examples.purpose: Use a documentation comment identifier when the symbol identity is already known.
examples.expectedOutcome: A bounded set of references is resolved for the selected symbol in the sample workspace.

examples.workflowTitle: Stage, review and commit one change
examples.title: Start a transaction
examples.purpose: Create an isolated staging area before invoking a mutation or Code Action.
examples.expectedOutcome: The sample workspace owns a new transaction at its initial revision.

examples.workflowTitle: Stage, review and commit one change
examples.title: Stage document formatting
examples.purpose: Stage a concrete source change inside the active transaction before reviewing it.
examples.expectedOutcome: Formatting is staged without writing the source file and advances the transaction revision.

examples.workflowTitle: Stage, review and commit one change
examples.title: Preview staged changes
examples.purpose: Inspect a focused diff before deciding whether to commit or roll back the transaction.
examples.expectedOutcome: A three-line-context diff is returned for the selected document without writing files.

examples.workflowTitle: Stage, review and commit one change
examples.title: Commit the reviewed snapshot
examples.purpose: Write the staged files only when the transaction still matches the previewed snapshot.
examples.expectedOutcome: The commit succeeds only if the supplied snapshot still identifies the current staged revision.

error.message: The staged transaction no longer matches the expected snapshot.

continuation.instruction: Preview the current staged revision and ask the user to review it before committing.

examples.workflowTitle: Discover and stage a Code Action
examples.title: Start a transaction for the Code Action
examples.purpose: Create the transaction that will receive the selected Code Action changes.
examples.expectedOutcome: The sample workspace owns a new transaction at its initial revision.

examples.workflowTitle: Discover and stage a Code Action
examples.title: Discover Code Actions
examples.purpose: List bounded fixes and refactorings against an exact document snapshot.
examples.expectedOutcome: At most 20 snapshot-bound Code Action references are returned for the selected document.

examples.workflowTitle: Discover and stage a Code Action
examples.title: Stage a selected Code Action
examples.purpose: Replay the selected action against its original snapshot and stage the resulting source changes.
examples.expectedOutcome: The action is replayed against the exact snapshot and its changes advance the active transaction revision.

examples.workflowTitle: Review and submit an error report
examples.title: Prepare an error report for review
examples.purpose: Create the immutable review payload before asking the user whether it may be submitted.
examples.expectedOutcome: A temporary reviewed submission handle and payload preview are returned without network activity.

examples.workflowTitle: Review and submit an error report
examples.title: Submit an approved error report
examples.purpose: Submit only the exact payload handle returned after user review and consent.
examples.expectedOutcome: The approved immutable payload is dispatched once, or a structured consent or availability outcome is returned.
